claims.text: Deep learning potentials can improve representation of atomic configurations in the ab initio liquid of multicomponent high-entropy alloys.
Improved representation by deep learning potentials will increase reference–target phase-space overlap.
Increased reference–target phase-space overlap will reduce thermodynamic-integration path mismatch relative to TOR-TILD's EAM references.
Deep learning potentials will improve prediction of thermodynamic properties.
The proposed intervention is applicable to solid and liquid multicomponent high-entropy alloys near their high melting temperatures.
Deep learning potentials are proposed as the single methodological intervention.
TOR-TILD's EAM references are the baseline against which path mismatch and thermodynamic predictions will be compared.
The hypothesis can be tested by comparing melting temperatures and thermodynamic properties predicted using deep learning potentials with those predicted using TOR-TILD's EAM references.
Failure to achieve a significant improvement in thermodynamic-property prediction relative to TOR-TILD's EAM references would falsify the hypothesis.
